deviations_from_the_spec: snap: the address filter uses two net.BlockList objects (one IPv4, one IPv6), not one. Node's BlockList checks an IPv4 address against IPv6 rules through its mapped form, so the spec's single list with ::ffff:0:0/96 would refuse every IPv4 address. I saw this in a test: 93.184.216.34 was refused.
Design vs contract: design R25 says snap fetches with 'Node's own fetch'. The spec and contract use http/https requests, each through its own Agent with a fixed lookup. I followed the spec.

Tamper record on exit 3: both scripts append the CONTRACT 1.4 tamper incident {class: refusal, detail: {tamper: true, script, code}} on object-mismatch and snapshot-mismatch, and witness also on card-changed. Not in dry-run, never for ledger-broken. I read the spec's 'nothing written' as no snapshot file and no witness record, with 1.4's incident line still applying.

schema_version: 1 is added to snapshot meta files and to witness.jsonl records, following CONTRACT section 3's 'every object carries schema_version', although the field lists in 3.13 and 3.14 leave it out. The witness stdout records leave it out.

snap: if raw/<sha> or text/<sha> already exists with other bytes, the script exits 3 `snapshot-mismatch`. The spec does not cover this case; createExclusive would otherwise give exists-different 1, and snap never exits 1.

snap: a URL that new URL() cannot parse gets reason bad-scheme and url_key null, and no by-url line is written. A DNS failure, a connection error, an unknown Content-Encoding or a decompression error each get reason http-error, since the enum has no closer slug.

snap: a by-url line with raw_sha null always has source_changed false. The spec's literal rule ('an earlier non-null raw_sha different from this one') would make a failed fetch true. by-url lines also carry `reason` when bytes were stored (pdf, unsupported-type, empty-text).

snap html-v1 choices the spec leaves open. Block tags (newline): address article aside blockquote body br caption dd details dialog div dl dt fieldset figcaption figure footer form h1-h6 head header hr html legend li main nav ol option p pre section summary table tbody tfoot thead title tr ul. td and th become a space, so ab gives 'a b'. Runs of newlines collapse to one, spaces next to a newline are removed, and the whole text is trimmed. `` and `` become a space. A self-closing drops only the tag. The charset is also taken from a meta http-equiv content. The fixed entity table holds about 100 names. Numeric references 128-159 decode as windows-1252.
snap: --root must be an absolute path (else 66, per CONTRACT 1.1). A malformed --now (not ISO 8601 with a zone) also exits 66.

witness numbers: a '-' or '+' directly after a letter or digit is a hyphen, not a sign (COVID-19, 3-5 still give 19 and 5). A token followed by '%' or 'percent' does not match when the unit is not a percent. Percent units: %, percent, per cent, pct, percentage, percentage point(s), percent points, pp, p.p., % points. Among bound tokens the nearest to the quote is reported. Value 3 does not match an explicit '-3'.

witness: the address-style stricter cases. A measured.value that is neither a number nor 'not stated' is rejected as number-missing. A number-without-quote record carries number_offset. Normalised quote matching is a plain substring search, so an empty normalised quote is quote-missing.

witness ledger: each per-slug reason of the check line has detail = an array of card ids (the tms 'reopened' pattern). The range reason comes first. The stdout reasons start with a summary entry `rejected` (exit 1) or `unverifiable` (exit 2), then card-changed, then the per-slug groups.
snap: the address filter also checks the embedded IPv4 of IPv4-compatible ::/96 addresses. This is stricter than the spec and never allows anything the spec refuses.
lib_change_requests: tcb/thresholds.json (owned by U5c, not lib) lacks three names: fetch_max_redirects (snap), and lock_retries and proc_exe (both scripts, per CONTRACT 3.20 and 4.4). Until they are added, both scripts exit 2 `param-missing` on every non-dry run, and snap on every run.

paths(root): please export string keys `snapshots` (<root>/.snapshots), `objects` (<root>/store/objects) and `witness` (<root>/store/witness.jsonl). The scripts use these keys when they are strings, and otherwise build the CONTRACT 2 paths themselves.

runMain: the scripts return `dry_run: true|false` in fn's return object, next to exit, result and reasons. runMain should print it as the 1.3 top-level `dry_run`, or read --dry-run from argv. result also carries dry_run: true in dry runs.

withRunLock(root, {script, ce, proc, now, retries}, fn): please pass `retries` through to acquireLock. CONTRACT 4.4 lists no retries option on withRunLock, but scripts must pass threshold lock_retries.

Assumed synchronous, as the contract's return-value signatures suggest: createExclusive, readJson, readJsonl, appendJsonl, appendLedger, recordIncident, getObject, checkCe, thresholds().get, parseArgs, edgeFacts, urlKey, canonicalize, sha256hex, realProc. Both scripts call them inside a synchronous withRunLock callback. withRunLock itself is awaited, so either form works for it. If appendJsonl, appendLedger or recordIncident return promises, the callback would release the lock before they finish.

Assumed: `TcbError` is exported, as new TcbError(code, exit, detail). parseArgs type 'list' returns an array and 'int' an integer. edgeFacts(flags) with no proc returns {now} (a string, Date or number is accepted). createExclusive accepts a string or Buffer and returns 'created' or 'identical', with exists-different carrying code 'exists-different'. The scripts make the parent folders first. appendJsonl creates a missing file. readJson throws with exit 2 for missing or unparseable.
not_testable_without_the_app: Real web pages (needs-app 10, F5): html-v1 extraction quality on real sites, paywalls and challenge pages that answer 200 with a block page (stored as text and caught later as quote-missing), real PDFs, real charsets and encodings.
Real DNS answers, IPv6 resolution, and TLS (SNI and certificates) to real hosts through the fixed-lookup agents. The tests only reach 127.0.0.1.
That a real run's allow_loopback is false. Selftest's threshold check covers this, not snap.
The share of honest cards whose reader saw only a fetch summary and whose quote is a paraphrase (G7, number-without-quote), measured in the pilot.
How witness normalisation and number binding behave on real extracted texts (ligatures, hyphenation and number formats as real pages render them).
open_points: Not run end to end: lib.mjs did not exist while I worked, so the CLI flows have not run (locking, ledger lines, by-url and witness.jsonl appends, exit codes through runMain, ce checks). The checks that did run used an in-memory stub of lib and a 127.0.0.1 server inside the process, with no files written. They passed: witness T1, T2, T3, T4, T5 (300 vs 301), T6, T7, T21; snap T3, T7, T8, T9, T10 (including the gzip bomb), T11, T12, T13, T14 (address table and the redirect to 10/8), T14b (global agent unused), T15, T16. Both files pass `node --check`.

Exports for the test writer. snap.mjs: addressVerdict(addr, {allowLoopback}) -> 'ok'|'private-address'; addressAllowed(addr, {allowLoopback}) -> bool (accepts [bracketed] IPv6); embeddedIPv4(addr); extractHtml(buffer, contentType); htmlToText(string); decodeEntities(string); classifyBody(buffer, contentType) -> {text?, reason?, extractor?}; fetchUrl(url, {maxBytes, timeoutMs, maxRedirects, allowLoopback, lookup?, onAgent?}) -> {finalUrl, status?, contentType?, body?, reason?}. onAgent receives each per-request Agent, for T14b. witness.mjs: normalize(s) -> {text, map} (map is an Int32Array; map[i] = UTF-16 index in s, map[text.length] = s.length); normalizeQuote(q); numberTokens(normText) -> [{start, end, text, sign, readings, percent}]; tokenMatches(token, value, unit); isPercentUnit(unit); witnessCard(card, text, w), also witnessCard({card, text, w}) -> {result, reason, number_bound, quote_offset?, number_offset?}. Neither module does anything on import; main runs only when the file is process.argv[1].

In the build the scripts sit at tcb/snap.mjs and tcb/witness.mjs, next to tcb/lib.mjs, and import './lib.mjs'. In a run root, CONTRACT 1.1 places them at tcb/scripts/; the relative import works there too if lib.mjs sits beside them.

snap fetches, then takes run.lock and writes, once per URL. A lock-busy (75) on any URL ends the run, keeping what earlier URLs wrote; a test that holds the lock from the start sees nothing written (T20). The F5 refusal (exit 2 f5-not-given) comes before checkCe, as the spec orders the steps; for --new its result.urls is built best-effort.

witness takes its decisions outside the lock (the last record per card, the skip check) and reads seq inside it. A second witness run in between could make a skip decision stale. Under the design's one-intake-at-a-time rule this should not happen.
